:::{#def-fitting-procedure}
#### Fitting procedure

A **fitting procedure** $\fitproc$ is a rule that,
given any data $\paren{(\predvar_{\iobs}, \outvar_{\iobs})}_{\iobs \in \obsidx}$ and any [covariate](#def-covariate) value $\predvar$,
computes a [prediction](prediction.qmd#def-prediction) of the outcome at $\predvar$:

$$
\paren{\predvar; \paren{(\predvar_{\iobs}, \outvar_{\iobs})}_{\iobs \in \obsidx}}
\mapsto
\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \paren{(\predvar_{\iobs}, \outvar_{\iobs})}_{\iobs \in \obsidx}}.
$$ {#eq-fitting-procedure}

It is specified by these inputs:

- the [data set](#def-data-set) $\dataset$ it is fitted to;
- the [model family](#def-model-family) $\modelfam$ of candidates it searches;
- the [objective function](#def-objective-function) $\objfn$ that scores each candidate;
- the [optimization algorithm](#def-optimization-algorithm) $\optalg$ that searches the family for a candidate with a good score;
- the [random seed](#def-random-seed) $\seed$, when the algorithm draws random numbers, as in splitting the data;
- the [tuning parameters](#def-tuning-parameter) $\tuning$, which it does not compute from the data;
- the [preprocessing](#def-preprocessing) $\featmap$ of the covariates.

:::
